correctness.rationale: Every v_i is positive. If the center is zero, exactly one u_i is two and the arm lower bounds give 3q+1. If the center is one, every arm costs at least three. If the center is two, a zero u_i forces the exact local minimum state (0,1,1), while a positive u_i costs at least three; the center requires a positive support neighbor, so at least one arm has the higher cost. For q>=3 this uniquely selects the center-two case at value 2q+3. Equality forces one exceptional arm of state (1,1,1) or (1,2,0). Definition-level exhaustive computation for q=3,4 matches both the minimum and complete optimizer classification.

value.rationale: The initiating paper singles out the once-subdivided star as an order-extremal total-perfect-Roman family. The twice-subdivided star is the immediate natural repeated-subdivision test. The theorem shows that this single additional subdivision changes the behavior sharply: on order 3q+1 the optimum is 2q+3, creating an exact q-2 deficit from the maximum, and all minima collapse to two local exceptional-arm states. This is a motivated structural boundary result rather than an arbitrary finite slice or routine numerical recomputation.
